Committee: Ways and Means Education
Sponsor: Garrett
Analyst: Jessica Perez
Date: 03/09/2021
FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 174 as introduced would exempt TWG 2021 Birmingham Foundation from the payment and collection of all state, county, and municipal sales and use taxes which would decrease potential receipts to the following funds by the following estimated amounts:
Education Trust Fund
$740,000
County Funds
$185,000
Municipal Funds
$740,000
Total
$1,665,000
Further, this bill would also exempt TWG 2021 Birmingham Foundation from the payment and collection of all state, county, and municipal Ad valorem taxes, which would decrease receipts to the following funds by the following estimated amounts:
State General Fund
$540
Public School Fund
$180
Soldier Fund
$450
County Funds
$2,430
Municipal Funds
$5,130
Total
$8,730
Additionally, this bill exempts any taxes with respect to the purchase or use of property and the gross proceeds from the sale or use of property by TWG 2021 Birmingham Foundation, which would further decrease potential receipts to the State General Fund, Veterans Assistance Fund, and county and municipal funds by an undetermined amount, depending upon: (1) the value of property obtained by TWG 2021 Birmingham Foundation; and (2) the amount of land used by TWG 2021 Birmingham Foundation.
Additionally, this bill would exempt TWG 2021 Birmingham Foundation from any licenses tax, which would decrease potential receipts to the State General Fund and county funds by an estimated $10,000 dependent upon the number of licenses required to be filed by the Foundation.
All exemptions provided in this bill expire on December 31,2023.
Bill Poole, Chair
Ways and Means Education

Committee: Ways and Means Education
Sponsor: Barfoot
Analyst: John Friedenreich
Date: 02/22/2021
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 106 as passed the Senate increases the compensation for surviving dependents of Alabama National Guardsmen from $10,000 to $100,000. This could increase the obligations of the State General Fund by an undetermined amount dependent upon the number of Alabama National Guardsmen killed while on state active duty status. Additionally, this bill expands educational benefits provided by the Alabama G.I. and Dependents Educational Benefit Act to dependents of Alabama National Guard members killed while on state active duty status. This could increase the obligations of the Education Trust Fund by an undetermined amount dependent on the number of claims for benefits by eligible dependents of Alabama National Guard members killed while on state active duty status.
Bill Poole, Chair
Ways and Means Education
